data.name: Amanisha
data.gender_notes: Amanisha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Amanisha is derived from the Sanskrit language. It is composed of two parts: ‘Ama’ meaning immortal or enduring, and ‘Nisha’ meaning night or rest. This name signifies one who is everlasting and enduring, like the night that never ends. The name Amanisha carries the meaning “Immortal, Enduring, Everlasting” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amanisha usually hope their child will grow to embody immortal, enduring, everlasting and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies the eternal and divine nature of the soul.
data.etymology: Amanisha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Immortal, Enduring, Everlasting.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amanisha total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Amanisha holds a significant cultural impact in Indian society, where the concept of immortality is deeply rooted in various Hindu mythologies and scriptures. The use of the Sanskrit language in this name adds to its ethereal and classic appeal, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of India. This name is also symbolic of the belief in fate and destiny that is deeply embedded in Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Amanisha lies in its symbolism of the eternal, unchanging nature of the soul. It is a reminder of the continuity of life beyond physical existence and emphasizes the value of endurance and perseverance in the face of challenges and hardships. The name also represents the idea of finding peace and rest in the divine, just like the comfort and security one feels during the night. Ultimately, it is a name that inspires hope and empowers individuals to strive for a meaningful and enduring existence.

historical_references.reference: Amanisha was an ancient Indian sage, who is said to have lived during the late Vedic period (around 500 BCE). He is known for his teachings on self-realization and the ultimate truth of the universe, which were recorded in the Upanishads.
historical_references.context: Ancient Indian sage, teachings on self-realization and the ultimate truth of the universe, recorded in the Upanishads

historical_references.reference: Amanisha is also mentioned in the Puranas, a set of Indian mythological texts, as a sage who attained enlightenment through deep meditation and devotion to Lord Vishnu. He is believed to have lived during the early medieval period (around 600-1300 CE).
